title: Access, roles and sharing: ideas from other products
intro: This is an internal board for the Essentials 2.0 solution concept. It is about how products solve problems, not how their screens look. Each example shows how another product solves an access, role or sharing problem our customers actually have. That includes learners without logins, faculty who can only see their own students, and class lists that live in Canvas. It also covers eight global roles nobody needs, and recordings that should open and close on dates. There is one section per question. Every card says what we would take from the example. Examples of what not to copy are flagged. These are examples we gathered from the design reference libraries Mobbin and Refero, and we will cut them down before anything is shown outside the team.

questions.title: How do products let people in without creating accounts first (email sign-in link, guest access, or identity from single sign-on (SSO) or a learning management system (LMS))?
How is access limited by content (share a course or recording with a person or group) instead of by a global role?
How do products handle bulk class lists: CSV or LMS import, sync, and groups that keep changing until week one?
What is the smallest set of roles that still has a way to make an exception (owner, admin, member, guest, plus per-item overrides)?
How is access open only for a set period (release date, expiry, semester end, view-only links, revoke)?
How do products cut the extra steps at login and the dependence on account recovery?

references.title: Welcome back with magic link first
references.question: Q1
references.take: Better Stack puts the magic link (a sign-in link sent by email) as the main button, makes password a secondary text link, and keeps SSO in a separate block. Passwords become the exception.

references.title: Admin login settings in one page
references.question: Q1
references.take: Calendly puts SSO, user provisioning and domain control on a single Login admin page with tabs. Identity settings sit in one place.

references.title: Email-only passwordless login
references.question: Q1
references.take: Chargetrip signs people into Analytics with email alone, and the same form also creates the account. The 'check your email' step offers mail-client shortcuts and says 'Logging in...'.

references.title: Share a doc before signup
references.question: Q1
references.take: Coda can grant an email 'Can edit' before the person has an account, and shows a 'Hasn't signed up' badge until they arrive. That is how you attach a learner to a recording before they have a login.

references.title: Six-step magic-link login
references.question: Q1
references.take: Cushion runs a six-step magic-link login with separate 'sending link' and 'link sent' screens. That is the smallest passwordless loop we found.

references.title: Accept invite still forces password
references.question: Q1
references.take: What not to copy: 'Accept invite to view' still forces a full name plus a 12-character password with five complexity rules, for a viewer-only invite. Those extra steps are what produce lockouts.

references.title: One email for signup and magic link
references.question: Q1
references.take: Enode uses one email form for both sign-up and log-in via magic link, then shows an in-app 'Verify your log-in' confirmation before the dashboard.

references.title: Magic-link onboarding from marketing
references.question: Q1
references.take: Flask.do moves from a marketing button to an auth-method card, then email, then 'link sent', then an empty team workspace. It asks for nothing beyond an email.

references.title: Three-radio team login policy
references.question: Q1
references.take: Homerun offers three login policies (none, two-step sign-in or SSO, SSO only), each with consequence text. One control enforces the rule for the whole organisation.

references.title: Invite lands via temporary magic link
references.question: Q1
references.take: Jitter already knows the invite email, so 'Log in' sends a temporary magic link and drops the invitee straight into the team. No password is ever set up.

references.title: Login with Google, magic link and SSO
references.question: Q1
references.take: Linear's login screen offers Google, email magic link, a common single sign-on standard (SAML), and passkey as peers. The 'check your email' step has an 'enter code manually' fallback when links do not open.

references.title: Magic link as recovery path
references.question: Q1
references.take: Miro puts 'Trouble signing in? Request a magic sign-in link' next to reset-password, and 'sign in to a private organization' for SSO tenants. That answers the months-long lockout problem.

references.title: Continue as a visitor
references.question: Q1
references.take: Mural's visitor mode asks only for a display name on a shared board and lets the person in. That is the closest match to attaching a learner to a recording without an account.

references.title: Work email magic link into org setup
references.question: Q1
references.take: Parallel's 'Sign in with work email' magic link lands straight in org creation. Identity comes first, the workspace second, and there is no password anywhere.

references.title: One entry for sign in or create
references.question: Q1
references.take: Pitch says 'We'll sign you in or create an account if you don't have one yet'. One entry point collapses login and signup so the invitee never has to know which they need.

references.title: Email first, then SSO and org picker
references.question: Q1
references.take: Plain asks for email first, then 'Continue with SSO', then a 'Select an organization' picker. Identity comes from the org's sign-in system, the identity provider (IdP), and the user just chooses which tenant to enter.

references.title: Magic-link login end to end
references.question: Q1
references.take: Qatalog runs magic-link login end to end, including the email itself. The link expires in 20 minutes, is single use, and includes a copyable URL for signing in on a different device.

references.title: Invite acceptance is plain signup
references.question: Q1
references.take: What not to copy: invite acceptance is a plain signup form (name plus password) with the email pre-filled. The invite context buys nothing beyond the headline.

references.title: SSO settings for admins only
references.question: Q1
references.take: Slab's org SSO settings page shows 'no providers yet' with one 'Manage integrations' button. SSO is an admin toggle and stays invisible to end users.

references.title: Domain auto-join plus magic link
references.question: Q1
references.take: Slite offers domain auto-join ('if you have an @school.edu address you can join this organization') plus a 'Send magic link' versus 'Type password' choice on the same email field.

references.title: Three ways to accept an invitation
references.question: Q1
references.take: Slite offers three ways in: a shareable join link ('anyone with this link can join'), import from Google or Slack contacts (a class-list source), or typed emails. The contact import is the Canvas-like pattern.

references.title: Set document access by attributes
references.question: Q2
references.take: Aboard limits access on a document with Workplace, Department and Role dropdowns instead of naming people. That maps to site, program and cohort for a sim center.

references.title: Project access settings and member roles
references.question: Q2
references.take: Asana puts a project-level 'Access settings' switch (My workspace versus Private to members) above a member list where each row has its own role (Project admin, Editor or Viewer).

references.title: Request access from project admins
references.question: Q2
references.take: When access is denied, Asana routes the request to the project's admins (not a global admin), with an optional message for the approver. Access limited to a project needs a request path limited the same way.

references.title: What one person can access
references.question: Q2
references.take: Basecamp flips the share dialog: a checklist of projects one person may see, with a plain-English 'what happens next'. That is a direct answer to 'faculty sees only their own students'.

references.title: Share dialog with link and roles
references.question: Q2
references.take: Bezi combines link-access choice, collaborator invite, and per-collaborator role change or remove in one share dialog.

references.title: Share folder to person or group
references.question: Q2
references.take: Cake Equity lets you share a document folder to a specific shareholder or group from the folder context menu. You pick a person or group, not a global role.

references.title: Video project share and link invite
references.question: Q2
references.take: Clipchamp's video-project share menu sends a link to recipients (with autosuggest) plus separate link settings. It includes share error and retry screens.

references.title: Per-user permission grid per space
references.question: Q2
references.take: What not to copy: Confluence shows a per-user grid of 15 checkbox columns (view, delete own, add, archive, export and more) with Users, Groups and Guests tabs. It is detailed but hard to read, and it applies per space rather than per content.

references.title: Folder manage-access dialog
references.question: Q2
references.take: Dropbox's folder 'Manage access' dialog has a per-collaborator permission selector and confirms the change on the same screen.

references.title: Collaborators versus readers tabs
references.question: Q2
references.take: ElevenLabs splits the audience into Collaborators versus Readers tabs, then stacks three audiences with their own level: named people, Workspace Access and Public Access.

references.title: Per-file share overrides team default
references.question: Q2
references.take: Figma's per-file share settings switch link access to 'Only invited people', then invite by email. Item-level access overrides the team default.

references.title: User groups for sharing meetings
references.question: Q2
references.take: Fireflies sells user groups as 'easily share meetings with a particular group'. Groups exist to receive recordings, not to hold a global role.

references.title: Five repository roles plus custom roles
references.question: Q2
references.take: GitHub offers five pre-defined roles, each described in one sentence as 'previous role plus X', applied per repository via teams. Custom roles are a way to make an exception, not the default.

references.title: Invite client with visible access
references.question: Q2
references.take: Hello Ivy's external-client invite lets you adjust what the client can see before sending. A pending invite shows in the client list.

references.title: Share project with re-share lock
references.question: Q2
references.take: Hex uses one input for 'users, groups, or collections'. The whole-workspace row is a toggle with its own level, and a 'prevent Can-edit users from re-sharing' checkbox stops privilege leaking.

references.title: Team-only versus anyone with link
references.question: Q2
references.take: Maze offers two radios for sharing a reel: 'Only members in your team' versus 'Anyone with the link'. That is the smallest audience choice for sharing a recording.

references.title: Groups as sharing targets
references.question: Q2
references.take: Notion's people table has Teamspaces, Groups and Role as separate columns, and a Groups tab that shows how many teamspaces each group unlocks. Groups are a sharing target; role stays small.

references.title: Share dialog by audience tab
references.question: Q2
references.take: Sketch organises the share dialog by audience tab: Workspace Members (Restricted), Guests, and Everyone (No Access). Being in the workspace does not mean seeing the document.

references.title: Invite with role and public link
references.question: Q2
references.take: Skiff's document dialog invites by email with a role, lists guests versus team members, and offers a public-link toggle. All of it applies to one document.

references.title: Global capability by role matrix
references.question: Q2
references.take: What not to copy: StackAI shows a global capability-by-role checkbox matrix (dozens of rows, 'Add Role' button). This is the eight-global-roles trap: it can never express 'only my students' videos'.

references.title: Guest invited to a single project
references.question: Q2
references.take: Synthesia invites a guest to a single project. A 'Review external access' step warns what they will see, then a permission level is chosen.

references.title: Community access by membership tier
references.question: Q2
references.take: Teachable limits a content area by audience: pick which membership tiers can access the community. That is cohort-based limiting for edtech.

references.title: Share video with collaborators and viewers
references.question: Q2
references.take: Vimeo's video share shows 'All admins - Can manage' as an implicit row, the owner, a named person with Can comment, and a separate Link privacy control. Collaborators versus Viewers are counted in the comments panel.

references.title: CSV import with column mapping
references.question: Q3
references.take: Acuity Scheduling's CSV import shows a 'mapping required' preview and applies column labels before a success banner on the client list.

references.title: Bulk stakeholder import with validation
references.question: Q3
references.take: Cake Equity auto-maps columns on upload, then validates on import with row-level errors before committing.

references.title: Admin groups by department
references.question: Q3
references.take: Calendly's admin Groups area organises members by department or location with group admins. That is cohort structure with delegated admin.

references.title: Add selected people to a group
references.question: Q3
references.take: Canva lets you multi-select people in the member list and choose 'Add to group'. Groups and cohorts are built from people who are already there.

references.title: SSO and provisioning beside domain check
references.question: Q3
references.take: Canva's 'SSO & provisioning' settings include a domain-verification tab. Directory sync (automatic copying of people and groups from another system) sits next to SSO, not as a separate product.

references.title: Invite with manual or CSV import
references.question: Q3
references.take: Circle puts 'Enter manually | Import CSV' as a toggle inside the Invite flow, with a template CSV link and tag assignment for the batch. That answers the 'batch upload existed but nobody found it' problem.

references.title: Bulk CSV import with logs
references.question: Q3
references.take: Circle's bulk import shows the invite email preview before upload, then a 'Bulk logs' table (Pending to Completed, input plus output CSV) so a tech can verify what landed.

references.title: Upload, map fields, review cohort
references.question: Q3
references.take: Customer.io runs a three-step Upload, Map fields, Review flow. The review screen counts new versus existing people, warnings and errors, and offers 'add these people to a new or existing segment', so import creates the cohort in one go.

references.title: Four-stage CSV bulk edit flow
references.question: Q3
references.take: What not to copy: Deel's download-edit-upload-validate-choose-review flow is a four-stage full-screen process. It fits 300 payroll records, and is far too heavy for a sim tech adding a group of 4 to 10 learners.

references.title: Members list with status and groups
references.question: Q3
references.take: Dropbox's admin members table has a status filter (invited or active) and Groups as a sibling nav item. The class list and cohorts live in one console.

references.title: Create group by picker or CSV
references.question: Q3
references.take: Front's create-group form offers both a checkbox picker of existing people and 'Download CSV template / Import CSV' on the same screen. Small groups by hand, big cohorts by file.

references.title: CSV import with column mapping table
references.question: Q3
references.take: Ghost's CSV import uses a column-mapping table (field, sample data, import as), updates existing people on matching email, and auto-labels the batch 'Import <date>' so the cohort is findable afterwards.

references.title: Add, bulk upload and download members
references.question: Q3
references.take: Google Workspace puts Add members, Bulk upload members and Download members side by side on the group page, and separates direct versus indirect (nested) members. That is a model for cohorts that contain sub-groups.

references.title: Invite dialog with import nudge
references.question: Q3
references.take: Grammarly's invite dialog puts bulk import as a one-line nudge under the email box ('Want to add emails in bulk? Import list') plus a domain-restricted join link. Bulk stays discoverable without a separate feature.

references.title: CSV user import with report
references.question: Q3
references.take: Intercom's import flow maps each CSV column to a user attribute, then ends with a post-import report of created, updated and failed rows.

references.title: Paste emails and add to team
references.question: Q3
references.take: Linear lets you paste comma-separated emails plus an optional 'Add to team' in one dialog. Invitees appear at once in the members table with '(Invited)' status and their team, so the class list exists before anyone accepts.

references.title: Paste multiple emails to invite
references.question: Q3
references.take: Miro's invite uses a multiline paste box for bulk emails with an 'add individually' fallback. One field handles 1 or 100 invites.

references.title: Canonical CSV import flow
references.question: Q3
references.take: Resend shows the standard CSV import: upload, map columns (auto then manual), review parsed rows, an importing indicator, then the list.

references.title: Join link, contacts or typed emails
references.question: Q3
references.take: Slite stacks three entry paths on one card: join link, pull from Google or Slack contacts, or type emails. A join link or code is the cheapest answer when a cohort keeps changing until week one (learners enrol themselves).

references.title: Add student and enroll in one step
references.question: Q3
references.take: Teachable adds students manually with an 'enroll in course' toggle in the same dialog, then shows import feedback and an updated class list.

references.title: Invite with email or CSV upload
references.question: Q3
references.take: Uber Eats uses the same invite dialog for manual emails or CSV upload. It shows a format error and an 'imported 0 of 5' review list so you can fix rows.

references.title: Sync from email list or upload CSV
references.question: Q3
references.take: Vimeo's registrants header offers 'Sync from email list' next to 'Upload CSV' with in-page progress. Sync (continuous, from a source of truth) and upload (one-off) are distinct verbs, matching a student information system (SIS) or Canvas versus a spreadsheet.

references.title: Change member permission in the row
references.question: Q4
references.take: Ballpark lets you change a member's permission from the row with a selector and confirm inline. There is no separate edit page.

references.title: Separate Guests area for externals
references.question: Q4
references.take: Ballpark keeps a separate 'Guests' area for external people with a restricted role. Guest access is a clear, bounded role of its own.

references.title: Share dialog with stacked audiences
references.question: Q4
references.take: Coda's share dialog stacks audience rows for anyone with the link, anyone in the workspace, inherited from folder (greyed out), and named people. Each row has Can view, comment, edit, or No access, and inherited rows stay locked.

references.title: Invite with role help explainer
references.question: Q4
references.take: Column puts a role dropdown and a 'Roles help' explainer inside the invite dialog. The pending invites list updates in place.

references.title: Per-project roles override workspace
references.question: Q4
references.take: Descript lets per-project collaborator roles override the workspace role. That is a way to make an exception on one item next to a small global role set.

references.title: Three roles with inline descriptions
references.question: Q4
references.take: Expensify offers three roles (Employee, Auditor, Admin) as a segmented control, with the selected role's description underneath. The members table also has 'Import from spreadsheet' and a join link in the header.

references.title: Vague permission level names
references.question: Q4
references.take: What not to copy: permission levels named Basic, Low, Med and High carry no meaning. The admin must read the whole grid to know what 'Med' does. Role names should describe a job, not a rank.

references.title: Two roles Admin and Member
references.question: Q4
references.take: Gamma keeps exactly two roles (Admin and Member), each with a one-line description in the dropdown, plus 'Remove from workspace' as the third option. Role changes are a single click with no confirm step.

references.title: Inherited org access plus per-person
references.question: Q4
references.take: GitBook labels the org-wide row as 'Inherited' with a member count, while a named person can have an explicit 'Administrator' override. A toggle can also mint a guest link with its own role. Three layers sit in one small panel.

references.title: Convert member to guest inline
references.question: Q4
references.take: Height splits the Users page into Invited, Guests and Members sections. A role cell offers 'Convert to guest', 'Convert to admin' or 'Remove' with a light inline confirm. Guest is a conversion, not a separate account type.

references.title: Guest badge on share panel
references.question: Q4
references.take: Notion adds a per-item way to make an exception on top of workspace roles. The Share panel lists people (with a 'Guest' badge), the teamspace, and 'General access: Everyone at <workspace>', each with its own Full access, Can edit or Can comment level.

references.title: Four-role ladder at invite time
references.question: Q4
references.take: Obvious shows the four-role ladder with descriptions inline at invite time. Guest is 'only projects they're invited to', Member can 'create and access projects', Admin can 'manage members and settings', and Owner handles 'billing and transfer'.

references.title: Eight-step permission checklist
references.question: Q4
references.take: What not to copy: Pinterest asks for a role choice, then per-business, then a per-permission checklist. That is eight steps to add one employee, and the matrix keeps growing.

references.title: Role cards with View Edit columns
references.question: Q4
references.take: Remote shows roles as cards with plain-language descriptions and head counts, plus a dashed 'Add new role' card as a way to make an exception. Custom role permissions are grouped by AREA with just View and Edit columns, not per-action toggles.

references.title: Invite with role descriptions panel
references.question: Q4
references.take: Replo's invite dialog has an expandable 'view role descriptions' panel so people pick the right role without leaving the flow.

references.title: Three-dimensional permission groups
references.question: Q4
references.take: What not to copy: Retool's 'Permission groups' each track apps, resources and users. An admin must reason about a three-dimensional matrix to answer who can see something.

references.title: Guest invite with channels and expiry
references.question: Q4
references.take: When Slack switches 'Invite as' to Guest, it progressively reveals required channels and an expiration date. A guest is limited to content and open only for a set period. That fits simulated patients or visiting faculty without a dedicated global role.

references.title: Roles by permissions checkbox matrix
references.question: Q4
references.take: What not to copy: StackAI uses a roles-by-permissions checkbox matrix that gains a column per role and a row per action. Adding 'Contributor' means checking about 30 cells. This is what eight global roles turns into.

references.title: Role chosen at invite time
references.question: Q4
references.take: Stripe chooses the role at invite time from a short fixed list with one-line descriptions. There is no separate role-admin step.

references.title: Members and Guests as tabs
references.question: Q4
references.take: Synthesia.io splits workspace people into Members and Guests tabs. Each row shows role and license. Guest is a tab, not a column in a role matrix.

references.title: Fixed roles with View permissions
references.question: Q4
references.take: Teachable uses a fixed role list (Primary Owner, Owner, Author, Affiliate) with a 'View permissions' expander. The set is small and fully transparent.

references.title: Downgrade member to guest confirm
references.question: Q4
references.take: Twist opens a confirm when you downgrade Member to Guest. It spells out the consequences ('can only access channels they've been invited to, can't invite members') and asks for an explicit 'Yes, I'm absolutely sure' checkbox.

references.title: Per-member roles and access page
references.question: Q4
references.take: Zendesk gives each member a 'roles and access' page: one role plus product-level access toggles. The way to make an exception lives on the person, not in a matrix.

references.title: Track share and invite link controls
references.question: Q5
references.take: This untitled media product puts invite-only versus public, allow downloads, and password-protect in one panel. Link controls for media sit together.

references.title: Reset share link to revoke
references.question: Q5
references.take: This untitled product resets the share link with a confirmation dialog. The old link dies and a new one is issued. That is the simplest revoke pattern.

references.title: Link expires after and available to
references.question: Q5
references.take: 1Password covers expiry and audience with two dropdowns: 'Link expires after' and 'Available to' (anyone or specific emails).

references.title: View-only link with LIVE badge
references.question: Q5
references.take: Adobe Express frames a view-only link as 'allows anyone to see the file, no sign-in required'. It shows a LIVE badge, a preview of what recipients will see, a password toggle, and Delete link or Update link.

references.title: Board link name email and expiry
references.question: Q5
references.take: Air's board share settings include 'Require name and email to view' (light identification without an account), passcode, and expiration date. Each is an independent toggle.

references.title: Public link on its own tab
references.question: Q5
references.take: Airtable keeps the public link on its own 'Share publicly' tab, configured separately from collaborator invites.

references.title: Switch to link and set permission
references.question: Q5
references.take: Canva lets you switch from restricted to link-based access and choose the link's permission level in the same step, then copy.

references.title: Overkill checklist with countdown
references.question: Q5
references.take: What not to copy: Cloaked's per-field permission checklist and 1-hour default expiry are overkill for training content. Keep the live '59 mins' countdown ring on the published-link screen, which makes the open-only-for-a-set-period window visible.

references.title: Publish link with expiration stack
references.question: Q5
references.take: Craft's publish-to-web panel lists Password, Email access and Expiration as one stack of settings with 'Never' defaults. The calendar offers 'Expire on Thu, Apr 30' versus 'Never expires'. A single Unpublish button revokes, and a viewer count shows who used the link.

references.title: Edit and view links with expiry
references.question: Q5
references.take: Dropbox separates 'Link for editing' and 'Link for viewing' tabs, each with its own expiration toggle and date, password and download controls. 'Restrictions apply - Modify' shows the constraint next to Copy link. 'Unshare file' is the revoke-all action.

references.title: Link settings as three questions
references.question: Q5
references.take: Figma breaks link settings into three questions: Who can access, What can they do (View vs Edit), and Additional security. A note says link settings do not override people already invited directly.

references.title: Schedule membership post publish
references.question: Q5
references.take: Fourthwall lets you schedule a membership post's publication date and time from the post editor. That is scheduled publish for limited-access content.

references.title: Video share expiry presets
references.question: Q5
references.take: Frame.io's video share panel offers expiry with quick presets (24h, 1 week, 2 weeks) plus an exact date and time. It also has a passphrase toggle, and shows the resulting expiry inline as 'Dec 31 at 11:59pm' with Edit.

references.title: Schedule post with plain confirmation
references.question: Q5
references.take: Ghost's publish step is a plain-language sentence ('Set it live now' versus 'Schedule for later' plus date and time). A confirmation says 'Your post will be published on October 25th at 01:42', with a one-click 'Unschedule and revert to draft' undo.

references.title: Invite link with role limit expiry
references.question: Q5
references.take: Hashnode's admin-created invite link carries a role, a usage limit and an expiry date. That is cohort self-enrolment with a built-in shelf life.

references.title: Anyone or chosen people with expiry
references.question: Q5
references.take: Microsoft Loop follows the OneDrive and SharePoint model customers asked for. You pick the audience (Anyone, People you choose, or People with existing access), then Can edit level, expiry date, 'Require verification' and 'Set password' in one compact sheet.

references.title: Configure protections before link
references.question: Q5
references.take: MonoDesk has a 'Configure protections' step before the link is generated. Expiry and password are set up front, not as an afterthought.

references.title: Visitor link for people without accounts
references.question: Q5
references.take: Mural's 'Visitor link access' is a distinct tier for people without an account (anonymous learners). It has its own view or no-access level, optional password, and expiration shown as 'Expires Feb 28, 2025, 10:50 AM GMT-7'. 'Reset visitor link' revokes by rotating the URL without touching workspace members.

references.title: Security that burdens the sharer
references.question: Q5
references.take: What not to copy: NordLocker asks for a terms checkbox before generating a link, and a separate security code the sender must pass on outside the product. Expiry is fixed and you cannot change it, and the link is frozen to one file version. That security pushes work onto the sharer.

references.title: Stop sharing erases the link
references.question: Q5
references.take: Proton Drive writes revocation as a consequence, not a verb: 'Stop sharing - erase this link and remove everyone with access'. It sits under expiration date and link password toggles.

references.title: Edit link permission and expires after
references.question: Q5
references.take: Shuttle lets you edit an existing per-recipient link with a permission dropdown and 'Expires after'. Expiry stays editable after the link is created.

references.title: Lesson status Draft Published Scheduled
references.question: Q5
references.take: Squarespace course lessons carry a Draft, Published, Scheduled or Public preview status badge with a date. You can multi-select lessons and 'Set status for 2 selected' in bulk. That is the closest match to faculty releasing recordings on a date.

references.title: Password passkeys and sign out all
references.question: Q6
references.take: Canva's Login and security page manages password and passkeys side by side, plus 'sign out of all devices'.

references.title: Last used badge on sign-in method
references.question: Q6
references.take: Copy.ai puts a 'Last used' badge on the sign-in method you picked last time (email versus Google versus Microsoft). That removes the 'which account did I use?' guess that causes duplicate accounts and lockouts.

references.title: SSO email check with clear error
references.question: Q6
references.take: Epidemic Sound asks for email first, checks for SSO config, and shows a clear error when the domain has no SSO. That is email-first routing.

references.title: Managed inventory of recovery codes
references.question: Q6
references.take: Family's account recovery page lists masked recovery codes with remove and '+ New recovery code'. Recovery is a managed inventory.

references.title: Email sign-in with back to options
references.question: Q6
references.take: Hashnode offers 'Sign in with email' among several login options. The confirmation screen has 'Go to inbox' and an always-visible 'Back to login options' way out, so a user never gets stuck on one method.

references.title: Password or one-time code choice
references.question: Q6
references.take: After email, HBO Max lets you choose password or one-time code. Users can skip remembering a password without a reset.

references.title: Password reset via one-time code
references.question: Q6
references.take: IKEA resets the password via a one-time code typed inline, with no link to click. That means fewer context switches.

references.title: Google or email with no password
references.question: Q6
references.take: Lemni's entry is one Google button and one email field. There is no password to forget, no sign-up versus sign-in split, and 'Check your inbox' offers only Resend.

references.title: Offer passkey right after login
references.question: Q6
references.take: Link shows a 'Log in faster next time' banner right after a successful login, the moment to offer a passkey, with a dismiss control. It is never a blocking step.

references.title: Work email magic link with inbox buttons
references.question: Q6
references.take: Loops signs in with work email only and has no password field. After sending the sign-in link it offers 'Open your email client: Gmail / Outlook / Superhuman' buttons to finish in one click.

references.title: SSO with team identifier and error
references.question: Q6
references.take: Maze starts SSO with a team identifier and shows an explicit error when SSO initiation fails.

references.title: Passkey enrol after password and two-step
references.question: Q6
references.take: After password and two-step sign-in, multi-factor authentication (MFA), Mercury prompts passkey enrolment so the next login is one step.

references.title: Wrong password offers send a code
references.question: Q6
references.take: On a Microsoft account (the institution's own IdP), a wrong password shows 'Send a code to <email>' inline under Next. Hospital and university users already live in this pattern.

references.title: Full password recovery loop
references.question: Q6
references.take: Miro runs a complete recovery loop: error, then enter email, then loading, then 'instructions sent', then set new password, then back in.

references.title: MFA setup with recovery codes
references.question: Q6
references.take: n8n's MFA setup shows recovery codes and requires acknowledgement before finishing. Recovery is set up when access is set up.

references.title: One-time code beside wrong password
references.question: Q6
references.take: On 'Incorrect email address or password', OpenAI Platform offers 'Log in with a one-time code' as another path on the same screen. The reset itself is a 6-digit emailed code rather than a link.

references.title: Vague verify error forces reset
references.question: Q6
references.take: What not to copy: Paramount+ shows a vague 'Unable to verify your account' error. The only exit is Forgot password, then an emailed reset link, then a new password, then log in again. The whole session depends on the recovery email working.

references.title: Email code instead of reset link
references.question: Q6
references.take: On password mismatch, Patreon offers an email code instead of a reset link. It also handles an invalid code and retry.

references.title: Expired recovery link dead end
references.question: Q6
references.take: What not to copy: Sentry's expired-link dead end says 'link you followed is invalid, or it has expired' with only a text 'try again'. That is why sign-in links sent by email need a code fallback and a visible expiry.

references.title: Passkeys recommended plus secondary email
references.question: Q6
references.take: Shopify's Security page ranks Passkeys 'Recommended' above Password and explains it 'takes under a minute'. It also adds 'Secondary email - used to restore access' so recovery does not depend on one institutional mailbox.

references.title: Recovery key stuck on signup device
references.question: Q6
references.take: What not to copy: Skiff recovery depends on a key PDF saved on 'the device you used to sign up'. That hidden recovery dependency is what produces six-month lockouts, and the failure message gives no alternative.

references.title: Rate limit offers login with code
references.question: Q6
references.take: Surfshark's rate-limit dialog offers 'Login with code' as the main way out instead of a hard lockout. That is the direct antidote to months-long password lockouts.

references.title: Forgot password becomes passcode login
references.question: Q6
references.take: Turo rewrites 'forgot password' as 'Forgot password? Log in with passcode'. The recovery path is a login path (emailed code), so a forgotten password never blocks the session or requires a reset.

references.title: Passkey explained with recovery phone
references.question: Q6
references.take: Uber's passkey dialog explains in plain words what you will log in with (Face ID, Touch ID or Passcode). The Security page also lists Recovery phone as a backup channel and current login activity.

references.title: Six-digit email code login
references.question: Q6
references.take: v0 uses a one-time code instead of a link, which works when the email client is on another device. 'Use a different email' and a yellow nudge 'still waiting on your code? try signing up instead' handle the no-account case without a dead end.

references.title: Institutional paths plus instant email link
references.question: Q6
references.take: Workable's one screen offers every institutional path (Google, Microsoft, SSO) and 'Email me a link to sign in instantly' as a peer of the password button. A locked-out user has three ways in without support.
